key_insight: AutoPass uses evidence-guided multi-agent LLM reasoning to tune compiler optimizations by inspecting compiler internals and runtime feedback instead of treating the compiler as a black box.
engineering_relevance: This makes compiler performance tuning more adaptable to new codebases and hardware without offline training or task-specific fine-tuning.
method: Query compiler-internal optimization states and intermediate representations to inform LLM decisions.
Iteratively refine optimization settings using measured runtime feedback to detect regressions and improve latency.
Operate in an inference-only, training-free multi-agent workflow on LLVM.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on LLVM across server-grade x86-64 and embedded ARM64 systems, where it achieved geometric-mean speedups of 1.043x and 1.117x over -O3.
watch_item: Runtime measurements can be noisy and microarchitectural effects are complex, so the approach may be sensitive to benchmarking variance and hardware-specific behavior.
paper_title: AutoPass: Evidence-Guided LLM Agents for Compiler Performance Tuning
